title: I connected real CS2 and real Minecraft on a block-for-block Dust2. Here's how it works
author: LetOk3666
selftext:
**CrossDust** puts real Counter-Strike 2 and real Minecraft in one live match. CS2 players stay in CS2, Minecraft players stay in Minecraft, and they see and shoot each other on the same Dust2. Nobody installs client mods.

### How it works

* **Bridge:** one plugin on each game's server. They exchange text messages over local UDP, with player positions 20 times a second.
* **Map:** Dust2 rebuilt at 40 CS2 units per block. Stairs and ramps become slabs, so Minecraft players walk up them without jumping.
* **Players:** a CS2 player appears in Minecraft as a Mannequin with an agent skin. A Minecraft player appears in CS2 as a bot that the plugin teleports.
* **Damage:** each game owns its own player's HP. A hit is only a message to that game, and it decides when the player dies. 100 HP in CS2 equals 20 HP in Minecraft.
* **Look:** Minecraft downloads a server resource pack with CS2 weapons, Dust2 textures and agents.

### What doesn't work yet

* Blocks placed in Minecraft don't appear in CS2, so there's no building or breaking.
* Kills by Minecraft players don't count on the CS2 scoreboard.

The clip shows a scripted Minecraft client against CS2 bots on my test servers. A friend and I played an earlier build live, and human footage comes later.

Unofficial fan project, built with a lot of help from AI coding tools. Not affiliated with Valve, Mojang or Microsoft. It isn't for sale, and it isn't public because the map and pack come from game files.
